title: "Stage 7 – The menu and the public record"
case: trust
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at the menu](../../slides/trust-one-day.html#/the-specification-menu){target="_blank"}, in Part 3, in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

The last stage of the case works the menu and declares one analysis, as stage 4 did, and reads the public record of the paper. That record holds two careful rebuilds that drew the same variables from the same survey files and came out differently, a file prepared for the analysts that codes one variable the opposite way from the rule written above it, and two replications on later rounds of the survey. The module on repositories then shows how a public record keeps its versions, and the stage ends on the second case report. It takes about five and a quarter hours.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Case study](../../cases/trust/index.qmd#sec-reproduction), section 4 | The two reproductions that SCORE commissioned, each of which rebuilt the data from the ESS files, and why they part ways; the rebuild of the course; the file of the analysts, with its reversed dummy for the long-term countries of immigration and what it did to the interaction of Table 4 of the paper; and a slip in the record of Multi100. | 45 minutes |
| [Specification menu](../../cases/trust/menu.qmd) | The estimand statement, the twelve decisions at three levels, the five on which the curve keeps more than one option and the 192 specifications that they make, the worked example, and the rules for declaring and reporting. | 30 minutes |
| Slides, the menu in Part 3, and Task 4 in your report or working script | The ground rules of the menu, then `try_spec()` with no arguments and three or four times more, one argument at a time, compared with `my_experiments()`. Ask once for an option off the curve, such as `concern = "culture"`, to read why it is refused, and send the try that you would defend with `submit_exploration()` if you want it on the [class chart](../../cases/trust/multiverse.qmd#class-results). | 35 minutes |
| Slides, [Part 4](../../slides/trust-one-day.html#/part-4-multiverse-inference-and-preregistration){target="_blank"} | The class chart against the curve of 192, with the published result, the two SCORE reproductions, the five analysts and the two replications on it; what moved the estimate; standard errors with sixteen countries; and the two SCORE replications on later rounds. The critics of the multiverse and the slides on the archive repeat stage 4; skip them. | 30 minutes |
| The preregistration block in your report | Complete the block before you run anything: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, one option for each of the twelve decisions, a sentence from your causal graph on why the specification answers the claim, and your rule for what supports or undermines it. Render the report and keep the rendered copy, then fit the specification with `run_spec()`, and send it with `report_result()` if you want it on the chart. | 25 minutes |
| [Multiverse](../../cases/trust/multiverse.qmd) | Reading the curve, the reference marks, what moved the estimate, and the displays beside the curve: the options off the curve, the result with each country left out in turn, and the association between countries. | 35 minutes |
| [Case study](../../cases/trust/index.qmd#sec-replication), section 5 | The two replications on later rounds of the ESS, and why a replicated association still leaves its causal reading untested. | 15 minutes |
| [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd), [What a repository does](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-what), [The generalist repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-generalist), [The package of the housing-audit study](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-dataverse) and [Versions of a record](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-versions) | What a repository has to do, and the repositories that take any discipline; the package of the housing-audit study on the Harvard Dataverse, with its licence and its verification note; and how a record keeps its versions on the Dataverse, the OSF, Zenodo and git. Then open the dossier of this case on the OSF, from the note in [section 2 of the case study](../../cases/trust/index.qmd#sec-score), and find in it the two reproductions and the component of each analyst. | 65 minutes |
| Your report | Render the report with all five tasks complete, the preregistration as it stood before the run and the result beneath it. This is the second case report. | 30 minutes |

**Shortcuts.** If time is short, the displays beside the curve on the Multiverse page can wait. The case study and the repositories module carry the lesson of this stage, the difference between a result that comes back from the files of the analysts and one that comes back from the survey itself.

**By the end of the stage** you have your declared result placed among the 192 specifications of the curve, a preregistration that was completed before its specification ran, the second case report rendered, and a paragraph on what the two rebuilds and the file of the analysts show about reproducing a result from the files of a survey.
